gen-gf-gochi-hand-manrope: Manrope leaves a bright gap at the mouth of every curve and traces its whole line with one stylus width. Gochi Hand's crowded scrawl stays friendly; Manrope tidies up casual reading.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-fs-public-sans: Rope-thick curves with no stroke variation make Gveret Levin instantly recognizable. Public Sans adds a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, and the shared heft is what holds this pair together for brief bursts of text.
gen-gf-hachi-maru-pop-fs-neco: Relaxed, stretched-out spacing and an e that opens to the right give Hachi Maru Pop its hand-drawn ease. Neco swells gently from hairline to stem and never pinches shut, giving brief reading a dignified, authoritative tone.
gen-gf-hachi-maru-pop-fs-plein: Stretched-out spacing gives Hachi Maru Pop its loose, hand-drawn stride. Its wire-constant strokes are best at greeting a page warmly, while Plein, with a clear channel into each round letter, handles brief reading.
gen-gf-hachi-maru-pop-sora: Inviting and loose, Hachi Maru Pop spaces its letters far apart. Sora brings precise geometry and corners with no swell; that loose-versus-exact tension is the charm, comfortable for light reading.
gen-gf-hachi-maru-pop-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk breathes through open counters and builds each glyph from a ribbon of constant width, geometric and plain-spoken. Hachi Maru Pop stretches out relaxed up top, and neither wants long paragraphs.
gen-gf-hanalei-fill-fs-paquito: Paquito is a friendly serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals. Hanalei Fill echoes that with stencil-cut small letters and unchanging pressure; the shared sameness of height is their strongest bond, good for a couple of lines.
gen-gf-handlee-archivo: Handlee gathers its letterforms tightly, with hairlines sturdy beside the stems, while Archivo opens its curves outward with a commanding x-height. Handlee earns its keep big and short; Archivo is comfortable in light reading.
gen-gf-handlee-fs-asap: Mild pen-like weight variation and tightly gathered letters give Handlee a casual, graceful hand, while Asap stays readable with open arcs. Next to Asap, Handlee feels like a handwritten note, comfortable for brief reading.
gen-gf-handlee-general-sans: A faint thick-thin rhythm, like crayon on rough paper, marks Handlee. General Sans moves with steady pressure and an x-height that fills the line, smooth going, though brief copy is where this pairing feels best.
